reviews.comment: Tsvetkova's lectures are decent at best. A lot of the learning is from the Zybook / online textbook so there's not much you really need from her nor much I can say about her. Though in hindsight that may be a good thing. The course is alright. Just read the Zybook and do a bunch of coding practice and you'll get through it.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: With Professor Tsvetkova it's usually a hit or miss... Try to get on her good side cause that's how you'll do better in her class. She was very condescending to struggling students and tends to pick favorites. Her homeworks are 6 hours each at least and she gave us three in a single week before midterms at some point. Students beware...

This is the second course I've taken with her and the second that I've failed. Her lectures are very detail-focused and difficult to follow unless you already know the material and what you're looking for. You will need lots of studying outside of the lectures just to understand the lectures, but once you understand the lectures you know everything
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a good teacher with a heavy accent that makes it a bit harder to understand sometimes. Nevertheless, the material she taught was relevant and her lectures were still helpful while also providing examples to help better understand it.

Very energetic, heavy accent but lecture is still very good, provides slides which are helpful.
Lots of zybook readings, labs, and quizzes but is honestly not bad. Also gives some extra credit.
Midterm exam is not too difficult, final exam is hard but more than possible to do decent in.
Put in the work, don't fall behind, and you can get the A.

Tsvetkova is a very caring professor who gives a lot of extra credit. Just do all of the labs and understand the concepts, you will get an A. The lectures are pretty okay, she just has an accent so its hard sometimes to understand (look at slides/zybooks for review). Probably my best professor this year.

Queenie single handedly made this class a lot better. Its a difficult topic with hard projects and tests, especially if you haven't ever coded before, but she is very understanding and willing to help you through it. She gives lots of extra credit that other professors don't, and is quick to let you make up assignments you missed.
She is so sweet! The class itself is very very very hard but she made it amazing. During the tests she was so positive and wanted us to succeed! Highly recommend!!!!!

She is a great professor, if you have to take this awful class, please have her as a teacher. She gives so much extra credit and truly cares about her students. I had a lot of friends whose teachers never gave any extra credit. I love her and she has to be one of my favorite teachers. I am terrible at coding (got a 29% on the final) and still got B

Tsvetkova is alright, as a lecturer she is quite hard to understand but her assignments aren't too difficult, the only thing you have to study for is the exams. The quizzes are easy and extra credit is in the textbook. I would recommend trying to code as much as possible, do the group assignments too and you will be more prepared for the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Galina is very helpful when approached. However, I couldn't see her when she was lecturing and it felt like she was yelling at me for an hour and a half. I recommend sitting near the front and talking to her. She had a LOT of extra credit available and assigned less than my friends professors for the same class.
ENGR 102 is just a weird class in general, she was a perfectly adequate professor who taught the material fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tsvetkova lectures can be a bit hard to follow, she has a noticeable accent and goes through material very quickly. You definitely have to spend time on your own to learn the material. She is a very caring professor though and wants her students to succeed.

I had zero coding experience coming into college and this professor made it even harder to learn. She has a very heavy Russian accent and can be hard to understand at times. She flies through lectures as if everyone understands and covers topics only once. It's like she seems to care, but assign loads of homework...
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Tsvetkova genuinely cares about her students. However, she has a very thick accent and is hard to understand and moves through material very fast. She doesn't explain the topics very clearly. She expects students to grasp new concepts quicker than most of us can. If you can at all, avoid taking her class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsvetkova offers a lot of hw, which have lots of grammar errors and can be confusing to understand. The lectures have lots of info, but her accent throws me off. The exams aren't easy if you don't look at the lecture slides. The group projects were helpful, but if most of your team doesn't know how to code, good luck! Grading takes forever.

Galina truly cares about her students, but sometimes her accent is a little hard to understand. She doesn't always explain things in the clearest manner because "Python is not her first language", but if you ask for help she will help you to the best of her ability. She is super sweet and the things she says crack me up. A character for sure.

Tsvetkova is an absolutely amazing professor, the class is very dense material wise, however she presents the material in a very easy to follow way and overall keeps class insanely engaging. Along with this she is extremely available outside of class to help on any questions you have.
Save yourself the time tears and money and take it with someone else.
Terrible teacher. Cant understand in person, or online. Gives 3 times the amount of work compared to others. Dont take.

Professor Tsvetkova's class was great. Your primary focus should be on the labs since this is where most of the work and grading content comes from. Pretty much everything else, except for the tests, are pretty easy to knock out. When taking notes to prepare for exams, I would recommend printing out the lecture slides before each class period.

I think the Prof Tsvetkova is really good. She gives you many resources and if you keep up with your work, you will have a good experience. However, her class structure is very confusing and she doesn't let you know what your expected to do. This is the TA's fault. Also, TA lectures are useless. I do not really know why it exists. Overall good prof

She was very nice, but she didnt make this class great for online learning. As someone with no coding experience, I had to learn everything on my own because lectures were unhelpful. It IS possible to get an A, but you will have to use outside resources and put in MANY hours a week to do so, so be prepared for that if you have her.

It's very possible to get an A or B easily in this class with this professor, but it will make you tear your hair out while doing it. Not for the difficulty, but for the lack of organization. Just do a intro to Python course before the class starts, so you can use your time to set straight deadlines and clear up the inevitable confusion on HW.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsvetkova. Where do I begin. She's very sweet and wants you to learn. Hardest class I've ever taken (lots of lab work for which we did not have groups, BUT I did actually learn the material, with help from the Academic Success Center). Slides and eCampus page are VERY disorganized. Good communicator through email; accent is difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsvetkova is not bad but there are better options for this class.

Last resort professor... she didnt adapt well to teaching online, which is ironic considering this is a coding class. Two words to describe her are vague and frustrating. The latter comes from the former, but is the ultimate feeling evoked by this class.

Tsvetkova is really sweet and funny, but the class can be very disorganized. She does try to make up for it with a discussion forum for questions though. The only real con is that we were the only class without lab groups which made our labs EXTREMELY hard and time consuming, but it better prepares you for your future I guess.

To me, it seemed like the professor's structure of the course was all over the place. Nothing stuck to the syllabus. Almost every assignment was variable to change at a moment's notice. Additionally, the prof was the only one that didn't have group projects online, which made it EXTREMELY hard to complete the labs. Granted, teaching online is tough
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class felt very disorganized. Additionally the lectures felt like they were unproductive and I didnt learn much from them. I essentially had to learn python on my own.

I came into this period of online learning and I took Tsvetkova as she had some good ratings, but DO NOT take her for online school. She is unorganized, SKIPS over slides during lecture has useless lectures that don't pertain to the week's homework, and changed how the homework was graded midway through the sem. My prior coding experience saved me.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you get Professor Tsvetkova during this period of online learning, change to another professor. Ecampus is very hard to navigate, and she does not have an organized calendar at all. Too much homework, multiple labs due the same day with multiple parts each. You have to teach yourself everything. Unlike other profs, its all individual work.

I'm taking this semester and it is WAY harder than any of my other classes. Lectures are only 50 mins a week and she hardly covers any material but still expects you to learn it so be ready to read the textbook. Realized mid semester she was giving too much hw to grade so she made the computer grade it with crazy criteria rather than give us less.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you have a choice, do not go with this prof. Lots of homework and I just want to learn python. Hard to understand, only one lecture per week, horrible online class structure, switches ways we submit homework and labs in the middle of semester for no reason at all. No calendar to reference, bad hours for labs, the TAs are doing their best but man
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Reading other review I though I was inline for a good class, however that was not the case. She has lectures once a week but they are extremely hard to follow due to her being completely unorganized and having a lack of communication. For someone with coding experience I had a leg up but this class would be a nightmare if I was going into it blind.

This professor has a heavy Russian accent. This professor only lectures once per week. This professor teaches a class, which has NO PREREQS, where students learn to code in Python. I have done nothing but struggle in this class, there is no option to get help, and this with covid online learning has made taking this class absolutely miserable. 0/10

The lecture part of class was not bad - not all that interesting at times but overall helpful and learned a variety of different engineering applications (excel, engineering ethics, etc). The lab portion of the class was more difficult and time consuming, but she did not teach that portion of the class. Make sure you study for pop quizzes.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loveee Galina. I took her class for ENGR 102 and ENGR 216 and I am so glad I did. She is very understanding and she is always willing to help you out. She is organized so understanding the material is not particularly difficult. I actually loved going to her class because she would make people participate which - for me- really helped.

Dr. Tsvetkova knows her material well, but some times can be very hard to understand. If you ever talk to her after class or during office hours she is very caring and wants to help. ENGR102 is a lab and homework mad house with tons of coding/python labs, so get ready. The quizzes can be hard, but will prepare you for the final and midterm.

A real nice Russian lady who really knows her stuff! Exams cover what is in the exam review guides she gives out, and she posts her lecture slides after class. She has a slight accent, nothing bad. Go to lecture, she explains a lot there. She is also very liberal with partial credit. 10/10 overall

Galina was one of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. Her accent can be difficult to understand, but as long as you show interest in the material and do your work she will love you and help you out throughout the semester.

There is no one I love more than this woman. You begin every class with whatever one of her favorite videos she decides that day. You will be confused at first, but eventually you will just accept it and beg for more videos to be played every day. The class is hard if you are not good at coding, do the zybook and actually help with the projects.

She is a sweetheart, but she reads from the slides and goes through it really fast. In my opinion, her explanations aren't sufficient enough for the homework assignments. Her fast talking and accent combined made it really hard for me to understand what's going on. Google will be your friend if you don't have coding experience.

Honestly she is amazing, I wish she taught more of my nuclear classes. Her and Dr. Shao are the only professors whose classes I looked forward to. Her accent is understandable, and she gives us realistic expectations of what is needed from us. Only thing is I wished she didn't go so fast during lectures, she was blazing thru powerpoints.
Dr. G is probably the most chill professor that I have had. Occasionally I looked forward to going to class.
If she sees that you pay attention in lecture, she'll be really nice to you and help you out. Her tests are pretty easy and her accent is pretty understandable. I had a great time in her class!!

It wasn't too bad but the RATs are ridiculously difficult. I got a 89.56 and she still gave me a B. Somewhat bitter considering they lost one of my papers which would have gotten me an A without rounding. Disappointed in how long grading takes and how little the prof and TAs help.
She showed me the path to enlightenment. 11/10 would recommend, easy, fair grader

Enjoyed this class! Helped out when asked, held extra study sessions for those that wanted them. Responded to emails and was always helpful. Enjoyed the music she played for the class too! Overall an enjoyable class.
No one better at A&M to teach these classes.
OMG she is like the coolest prof ever. Be prepared for tons of fun and amazing videos that have nothing to do with engineering.
She is awesome. 10 out of 10 take again.

The professor really cares about the students and will set aside time after class to hold private review sessions any day of the week. She puts a lot of effort into preparing her students for the exams. Don't be afraid to ask her for any help because she is happy to do it.
needed google translate
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She has a an accent that is without a doubt hard to understand. As the semester goes you will get used to her accent. Its not that she doesn't teach, its that there is not enough time for her to teach, plus the course is very difficult. Go up to her and ask her to show you how to do the stuff she will actually help you and take her time to teach u
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: So like she doesn't teach, and she gives you homework based off things you haven't learned yet. You learn more from google than you do from the prof because she doesn't teach.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She reads off the slides and doesn't teach anything. It is up to the student to actually learn anything, and then the tests have nothing to do with what you were learning. Hard to understand what she is saying, definitely consider switching profs if you get her.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES
